Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan (post-call recap & next steps)

Hi Jordan & Priya - great to meet with you this morning. Thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have everything in the MAP for the technical evaluation milestone: 

Recap (from today’s discovery):
- Evaluation goal: confirm Redwood meets ACME’s latency and cost SLOs while preserving output quality for customer support summarization workflow.
- Primary stakeholders: Jordan (Eng/Infra), Priya (Product), Marissa (RD sales), Dylan (SE lead), Neha (AM).

Proposed MAP milestone: Technical evaluation plan
- Success criteria (benchmarks):
  * Quality: ROUGE/F1 on the ACME support corpus >= baseline (we'll use the sample prompt set you provided)
  * Latency: P95 end-to-end response <= 120 ms for a 512-token prompt (target)
  * Cost: average token cost <= $0.002/token during evaluation (estimate; will refine)
  * Throughput: sustained 30 req/s for single-region tests
- Model shortlist (initial): Llama-2-chat-70B (quantized), RedPajama-Chat-3B, and a smaller Claude-like  chat model for cost baseline. We'll confirm availability in our hosted catalog.
- Dependencies: access to a 1k-sample test set (can be synthetic), temporary test keys for a private eval cluster, and an agreed timeline for procurement/contracting.
- Owners & dates (proposed):
  * Redwood to deliver test harness + instructions - Dylan - target Mar 8
  * ACME to deliver sample dataset + access instructions - Jordan/Priya - target Mar 10
  * Run evaluation window - Mar 15-22
  * Review results & decide model variant - Mar 25
  * Target close for MAP (if evaluation successful) - Jun 30, 2027

I've attached a draft MAP sheet (ACME_MAP_DRAFT_v2.xlsx) with the above sketched in. Please confirm the success criteria and the target dates, and let me know any other dependencies I missed. If procurement pushes the target close date, call that out and we'll adjust.

Thanks - Marissa

--

- Latency: the 120 ms P95 target is for end-to-end inference within our network (including egress). Is that the same baseline you measured in the demo? We need to be careful about network variance.
- Cost target: ACME expects a production token cost closer to $0.0015/token; would Redwood be able to present a cost-optimized variant if we hit the quality bar?
- Security: please add the security checklist we discussed (SOC2 evidence, VPC peering options).

We can provide a synthetic dataset to start. Procurement will likely need the MAP and an SOW; procurement lead will review this week. If procurement is slow, we may need to push the target close date.

Thanks Jordan - good notes. I updated the MAP draft (v3) to call out the security checklist and a fallback cost target. Summary of updates inline here: 

Updated Success criteria (final for MAP):
- Quality: ACME sample set F1 >= current baseline (we'll capture baseline during first run).
- Latency: P95 end-to-end <= 120 ms (demo measured ~95 ms in-host; we'll instrument both sides).
- Cost: primary target <= $0.002/token, optimistic target $0.0015/token if we commit to a dedup/quantized variant.
- Throughput: 30 req/s sustained during throughput window.

Model shortlist (to validate during eval):
- Llama-2-chat-70B (quantized variants) - primary for quality/latency tradeoff
- RedPajama-Chat-3B - low-cost baseline
- Claude-like smaller chat model - baseline for safety/quality comparisons

Security & operations checklist (added to MAP):
- SOC 2 attestation (Redwood will provide certs)
- VPC peering or private endpoint for eval traffic
- Audit logs enabled for the evaluation cluster
- Data handling: synthetic sample set preferred; we can execute under NDA for real data if required

I've attached ACME_MAP_DRAFT_v3.xlsx with the updates and a short tech spec (redwood_tech_spec.pdf). Dylan - can you post the test harness instructions and confirm the Mar 15-22 window?

Thanks - Marissa

Subject: Test harness & runbook for ACME technical eval

Hi all - following up with the technical runbook for the evaluation. High-level plan and what we need from ACME to run the tests reliably: 

Test harness overview:
1) Redwood will provision a temporary dedicated eval cluster (single-region) with the following config: 2x A100-equivalent nodes, autoscaling disabled for deterministic latency.
2) We'll deploy candidates in parallel and run the following tests: latency microbench (P50/P95/P99), throughput ramp (to 30 req/s), and quality evals against the supplied prompt set.
3) We'll capture token-level cost estimates using our internal estimator and surface a projected per-token cost for the sustained window.

Dependencies / requests from ACME:
- Synthetic 1k sample set (JSONL) or a pointer to the dataset in a secure Drive location. Please redact PII.
- Temporary API key / test credentials or guidance for VPC peering (we can support either).
- Contact for SSO if you prefer team members to access our results dashboard (optional).

Deliverables & timeline:
- Test harness instructions (attached) - delivery: Mar 8 (done)
- ACME supplies dataset & credentials - requested by Mar 10
- Evaluation execution - Mar 15-22 (we'll run multiple seeds to reduce variance)
- Results deck & recommendations - Mar 25

Notes on hitting latency/cost targets:
- To meet P95 <= 120ms for 512-token prompts we recommend testing a quantized 70B variant + optimized attention kernels. If that fails, we will propose a smaller 30B quantized model or a caching strategy to meet the latency objective while preserving quality.
- Cost projections are estimates until we run the eval. We will include two cost scenarios in the results: hosted shared pool vs dedicated reserved capacity.

Attachment: redwood_test_harness_instructions.md

I'll stand up a short Zoom with Jordan/engineers the week of Mar 8 if needed to walk the runbook.

- Dylan
